accounts.prose: `catalog` exposes `lookup`, coordinating keyed retrieval rather than implementing storage or remote access itself. It rejects an empty key; on a cache hit it returns the stored value; on a miss it awaits `readRemote`, stores the returned value with `remember`, then returns it. Because storage occurs only after the awaited read completes, a rejected remote request is not cached. The nearby README describes the same sequence.

referent.description: The `catalog` module and its exported `lookup` operation.

qualifications: This is an interpretation of captured, first-observed source, not observed execution.
The README is attributed documentation; its applicability and truth are not independently established.
The available dependency analysis establishes source-level requests, not loader, deployment, or runtime availability.

accounts.prose: `cache` owns mutable in-process storage. `cached(key)` returns the value only when its sole entry has the same key; `remember(key, value)` replaces that entry. It is therefore a one-entry last-write cache, not a catalog replica.

referent.description: The cache module's lookup and replacement behavior.

qualifications: The entry is module-held state; its lifetime and sharing depend on the runtime's module-instance behavior, which was not observed.

accounts.prose: `remote` owns adapter selection and invocation. It starts with the name `./adapter`; `configureAdapter(name)` replaces that name, and `readRemote(key)` dynamically loads the currently named adapter and calls its `read(key)` operation. Thus transport, returned data, failures, and even the concrete adapter remain delegated beyond the analyzed modules.

referent.description: The remote-reader module's runtime-selectable adapter boundary.

qualifications: The computed dynamic import target is indeterminate to the available dependency analysis; adapter identity, interface compliance, availability, transport, and runtime behavior are not established.
This is an interpretation of captured, first-observed source, not observed execution.

Because storage occurs only after the awaited read completes, a rejected remote request is not cached. The nearby README describes the same sequence.

referent.description: The `catalog` module and its exported `lookup` operation.

qualifications: This is an interpretation of captured, first-observed source, not observed execution.
The README is attributed documentation; its applicability and truth are not independently established.
The available dependency analysis establishes source-level requests, not loader, deployment, or runtime availability.

accounts.prose: `remote` owns adapter selection and invocation. It starts with the name `./adapter`; `configureAdapter(name)` replaces that name, and `readRemote(key)` dynamically loads the currently named adapter and calls its `read(key)` operation. Thus transport, returned data, failures, and even the concrete adapter remain delegated beyond the analyzed modules.

referent.description: The remote-reader module's runtime-selectable adapter boundary.

qualifications: The computed dynamic import target is indeterminate to the available dependency analysis; adapter identity, interface compliance, availability, transport, and runtime behavior are not established.
This is an interpretation of captured, first-observed source, not observed execution.
